data.summary: In the gap between ddflow merge (lease released) and ddflow complete, ddflow next offers the merged item as ready and a claim by ANY other agent succeeds as a rework: item.reworked clears every gate, so the merging lane's complete is refused (implement, unit_tests, merge 'not run') and the second lane holds an empty item. Hit by 3 stub lanes in a sandbox in the first full run of SW-pilot-toy (toy-08: lane-1 merge 13:57:23, lane-2 claim 13:57:24 and item.reworked with the merged sha), and reproduced by hand with two agents: merge as lane-1, next as lane-2 lists it, claim as lane-2 exits 0, complete as lane-1 exits 3. Every parallel fleet has this race; any pull lane (SW-pull) makes it routine. The re-claim route of fix-B-rework-of-merged-item-keeps-stale-merge is for a deliberate rework. Direction: next does not offer an item with a merge and no completion, and a claim of one by an agent other than the merger is refused unless it says it means rework. Regression test: two agents, merge then next and claim, gates intact and complete passes. SW-pilot-toy works around it by never letting a lane claim an item another lane took in the run; real lanes share no such board.
data.title: A merged item not yet completed is offered and claimable: a second lane's claim wipes its gates

data.title: Fix bug B-merged-uncompleted-claimable: A merged item not yet completed is offered and claimable: a second lane's cla...

data.budget: 15 min, no live model, no GPU
data.claim: With stub workers, three lanes on the 12-item toy phase merge more than 1.8x the items per hour of one lane, all 12 on their gates with no override, and nothing reaches the host repository.
data.falsifier: A ratio near 1 at three lanes, an override or forced completion in the sandbox log, or a sandbox head known to the host.
data.mechanism: Each item's verbs run in its own worktree and only merge serialises on the sandbox main, so verb overhead (about 8 s per item) parallelises across lanes; a chain of 4 over 12 items leaves a ceiling of 3x.
data.probe: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py setup/run/report, one pair at --work-s 2 and one at --work-s 0, on this host at load average 75 to 117
data.probe_output: work-s 2: 387.88 -> 973.01 merged items per hour (2.51x), rework 8.33% both, agent-hours per item 0.0018 -> 0.0017. work-s 0: 459.52 -> 1248.92 (2.72x), rework 8.33% both, 0.0014 -> 0.0013. 12 of 12 merged, overrides 0, isolated true on all four sides. Stub time only: this measures ddflow overhead, not a pilot. First 3-lane attempt failed on B-merged-uncompleted-claimable (toy-08), filed; lanes now share a board.
data.question: Can a sandbox toy phase and one runner measure one lane against three through the real CLI, and is ddflow's own coordination a bottleneck at three lanes?

evidence.note: R20ea31dfa7 CONFIRMED: two stub pairs through the real CLI, 2.51x and 2.72x, 12 of 12 merged, overrides 0, isolated true; falsifier stated in the note.

d6fe74d8b: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py and swarm_pilot_run.py, ddflow metrics swarm view, provider wired through the shared Registry, compare leaves targets.cost None on agent-hours, research note. pytest tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py tests/test_swarm_metrics.py passes.

chunk_findings.detail: `agent_s = _held_s(ctx.facts, items, ctx.now) + _review_s(ctx.facts, items)` returns `0.0` when a repository has no `held` or `review` facts but has merged items (e.g., a sandbox/toy runner that records only completed states and no agent-hold records). The new metric `swarm.agent_hours_per_item` then emits `0.0` instead of `None`, and the new `text()` output prints `0.0000` under "agent-hours per item". That misrepresents absent measurement as a real zero agent-time figure; only `None` is rendered as `UNAVAILABLE`, so the view claims zero work was done rather than "unavailable", skewing the cost figure the change is supposed to model.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm_metrics.py provider

chunk_findings.detail: `judge` always returns `"compare": S.compare(before, after)` even when `comparable` is false. Concrete input: two sandboxes run with `--work-s 2` and `--work-s 4` produce a `why_not` entry for `work_s differs`, so the report says `"comparable": false`, but `report --json` still contains `compare.targets.throughput`, `compare.targets.rework`, and `compare.targets.cost` verdicts. A JSON consumer can read a target verdict for a pair the function says is not judged, contradicting the function's own contract and `render`'s human view.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:judge

chunk_findings.detail: There is no `lanes >= 1` validation. `python demos/swarm_pilot_run.py run DIR --lanes 0` (or a negative count) writes `lanes: 0` into the manifest, creates zero threads, sees no board failure, prints `ran 0 lane(s)`, and exits 0. This falsely records a sandbox as successfully run with no work done; the CLI should refuse non-positive lane counts.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: Unlike `guard_new`, `Sandbox.open` never rejects a path that is an ancestor of `ROOT`. Input: host repository is `[REDACTED:path]`; create `[REDACTED:path]` as its own git work tree with no remote and place `[REDACTED:path]` there. `Sandbox.open(Path("[REDACTED:path]"))` resolves the path, sees it is not inside the host, sees the manifest exists, passes `check()`, and returns a `Sandbox`. A subsequent `sb.ddflow("task", "add", ...)` runs `ddflow --repo [REDACTED:path]`, whose work tree contains the host repository, so the sandbox is not isolated from the host.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.open

chunk_findings.detail: The task-add loop adds every item with `--phase` and either `--needs <deps>` or `--tags no-deps`, but it never supplies a `wave:N` tag and never runs `ddflow waves --stamp`. This violates [r-task-phase-needs-wave], which requires every task to carry a `wave:N` tag; `no-deps` is not that wave tag. Running `setup()` on a fresh path creates 12 tasks without the required wave tag.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:setup

chunk_findings.detail: The documented agent-hours formula is “lease-held time plus recorded review time.” But the same document’s lane sequence is `claim`, `gate record` and `gate run`, `merge`, `complete`: a review recorded by `gate run` happens before `merge`, while the item is still lease-held. That review time is therefore already inside lease-held time, so adding it again double-counts it. Any real-lane run with a review gate (the setup this document explicitly tells SW-pilot-local to enable) inflates `swarm.agent_hours_per_item` and the `swarm_metrics.compare` `cost_x` ratio. The figure should not sum the two intervals; it should use a non-overlapping calculation such as lease-held time only, or subtract review time from lease-held time before adding it.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/swarm-pilot-toy.md:50

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `"cost_usd" in ans.text` only proves the label appears. A regressed view that still prints a skewed dollar figure (for example `cost_usd: 1.3`) when the log records no dollars would satisfy this test even though the comment claims it verifies “no dollars are recorded, and the view says so.” The test never asserts the value is `n/a` or absent, so the exact skewed-figure regression this change is meant to prevent is not caught.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_metrics.py:test_the_swarm_view_prints_the_baseline

chunk_findings.detail: `_git` runs `git -C <repo> ...` with whatever environment the pytest process inherited, without removing `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`. In an environment where these variables point at the host repository (the exact `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` attack the sandbox guard is supposed to neutralize), `git -C` does not override them. Concretely, in `test_a_linked_worktree_with_a_manifest_is_refused`, `_git(main, "worktree", "add", "-q", str(linked))` would add `<tmp>/linked` as a worktree of the **host** repository, mutating the host `.git/worktrees` metadata. This makes the new test suite itself touch the host under that environment, directly refuting the “sandbox never touches the host” guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py:_git

chunk_findings.detail: `_isolated` treats every non-zero `git cat-file -e` as "HEAD is unknown to the host". It also runs that probe with `env=sb.env`, so a sandbox env that makes host git fail (empty `PATH`, bad `GIT_EXEC_PATH`, `safe.directory` rejection, `GIT_DIR` pointing at a missing path) yields returncode 128/127, not 1. Given a sandbox whose `main` is a host commit and `git remote` is empty, `_isolated` returns True, `judge` sets `comparable`, and `render` can print throughput/rework `met` for a tree that is not isolated from the host.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:201

chunk_findings.detail: `run` builds lanes with `range(1, lanes + 1)` and treats an empty thread list as success. `python3 demos/swarm_pilot_run.py run DIR --lanes 0` (or `--lanes -1`) writes the manifest, starts no workers, never calls `Board.over`, leaves every item undone, and exits 0 with `ran 0 lane(s)`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:186

chunk_findings.detail: `Board.over` reads and sorts `self.left` outside `self.lock`, then calls `fail` before re-checking under the lock. If the deadline fires as the last lane `finish`es the last item, `over` still records `deadline: N item(s) left` and `run` raises `RunFailed` after a complete phase. Concurrent `discard` during `sorted(self.left)` can also raise `RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration` and fail the run the same way.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:122

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.__init__` stores any path and `git`/`ddflow` never call `check` or `guard_new`. `Sandbox(ROOT).must("merge", "toy-01")` runs `python -m ddflow --repo <host>` with the host checkout as `--repo`, so the sandbox harness mutates the host repository. The comments claim construction only through `setup`/`open`; that is not enforced on the methods that actually spawn processes.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:156

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.open` refuses a path inside the host but not a path that contains the host (`host.is_relative_to(real)` is only in `guard_new`). Given host `/work/proj` and an outer git repo `/work` with no remotes and `.ddflow/local/swarm-pilot.json` present, `Sandbox.open(Path("/work"))` succeeds, then `git`/`ddflow --repo /work` operate on a work tree that holds the host checkout.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:162

chunk_findings.detail: `clean_env` copies `TMPDIR` and `PATH` from the parent process. With `TMPDIR` set to a directory inside the host (for example `$HOST/tmp`) and `setup(Path("/tmp/pilot-sb"))` otherwise passing `guard_new`, `git` and the ddflow child still use that `TMPDIR` and can create files in the host. A `PATH` entry inside the host is also executed when resolving `git`/`python`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: `--lanes` is an unconstrained int. `run(sb, 0, worker)` (CLI: `run DIR --lanes 0`, also any `lanes < 1`) builds an empty thread list, never calls `Board.over`, leaves `board.failure` empty, and returns success after writing `lanes` into the manifest. The sandbox is then marked already-run, so a later real run is refused, while no item was claimed or merged.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: `over` reads and `sorted(self.left)` outside `self.lock` while `finish` discards from that set. With the deadline already passed and at least one item still in `left`, one lane in `over` and another in `finish` makes `sorted` raise `RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration`. That exception is caught in `_lane` and stored as the run failure, so a run that actually finished every item is reported as `RunFailed`. The same unlocked check can call `fail` after the last `finish`, which also sets `failure` on a completed board.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:Board.over

chunk_findings.detail: `_why_not` never requires the two sides to differ in `lanes`, and `judge` always attaches `S.compare` (including target booleans) even when `why_not` is non-empty. `report A B --json` therefore emits `compare.targets` as met/NOT MET for two equal-lane sandboxes, or for a pair with overrides / a non-isolated sandbox, while the text path prints `NOT COMPARABLE`. Swapping a 1-lane and a 3-lane directory judges the throughput target in the wrong direction with no refusal.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:judge

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.git` forwards every argument after `git -C <sandbox>`, and `check` only runs at open/setup, not on each call. `sb.git("--git-dir", "<host>/.git", "commit", ...)` (or `sb.git("config", "core.worktree", "<host>")` followed by a write) operates on the host repository even though path guards passed and the sandbox has no remote.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: `guard_new` refuses a directory that contains the host (`host.is_relative_to(real)`), but `open` does not. Given a parent of the host that is its own work tree, has `.ddflow/local/swarm-pilot.json`, and has no remotes, `open` succeeds; a later `git add` or task whose glob reaches the nested host tree writes the host checkout.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.open

chunk_findings.detail: The allow-list copies `TMPDIR` unchanged. With `TMPDIR` set to a directory inside the host repository, every sandbox `git`/`ddflow` process inherits that path and can create temp files in the host tree, which the “never touches the host” guard never checks.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:clean_env

chunk_findings.detail: `--lanes` is an unconstrained int. `run(sb, 0, worker)` (CLI: `run DIR --lanes 0`, also any `lanes < 1`) builds an empty thread list, never calls `Board.over`, leaves `board.failure` empty, and returns success after writing `lanes` into the manifest. The sandbox is then marked already-run, so a later real run is refused, while no item was claimed or merged.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: `over` reads and `sorted(self.left)` outside `self.lock` while `finish` discards from that set. With the deadline already passed and at least one item still in `left`, one lane in `over` and another in `finish` makes `sorted` raise `RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration`. That exception is caught in `_lane` and stored as the run failure, so a run that actually finished every item is reported as `RunFailed`. The same unlocked check can call `fail` after the last `finish`, which also sets `failure` on a completed board.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:Board.over

chunk_findings.detail: `_why_not` never requires the two sides to differ in `lanes`, and `judge` always attaches `S.compare` (including target booleans) even when `why_not` is non-empty. `report A B --json` therefore emits `compare.targets` as met/NOT MET for two equal-lane sandboxes, or for a pair with overrides / a non-isolated sandbox, while the text path prints `NOT COMPARABLE`. Swapping a 1-lane and a 3-lane directory judges the throughput target in the wrong direction with no refusal.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:judge

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.git` forwards every argument after `git -C <sandbox>`, and `check` only runs at open/setup, not on each call. `sb.git("--git-dir", "<host>/.git", "commit", ...)` (or `sb.git("config", "core.worktree", "<host>")` followed by a write) operates on the host repository even though path guards passed and the sandbox has no remote.

chunk_findings.detail: `guard_new` refuses a directory that contains the host (`host.is_relative_to(real)`), but `open` does not. Given a parent of the host that is its own work tree, has `.ddflow/local/swarm-pilot.json`, and has no remotes, `open` succeeds; a later `git add` or task whose glob reaches the nested host tree writes the host checkout.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.open

chunk_findings.detail: The allow-list copies `TMPDIR` unchanged. With `TMPDIR` set to a directory inside the host repository, every sandbox `git`/`ddflow` process inherits that path and can create temp files in the host tree, which the “never touches the host” guard never checks.

chunk_findings.detail: `open` passes the raw `path` to `cls`, and `__init__` resolves it only for `self.repo` (`self.repo = apart_from_host(repo)`), while `self.home` is still computed from the unresolved parameter `repo`. If `path` is a symlink inside the host repository that points to an external sandbox, `apart_from_host` accepts the resolved target, but `self.home` becomes `<host-dir>/<symlink-name>.home` inside the host. `clean_env` then sets both `HOME` and `TMPDIR` to that host path, so sandbox temp files can be written into the host tree despite the guard. Example: host `[REDACTED:path]`, symlink `[REDACTED:path] -> /srv/sbx/repo`, valid manifest at the target; `Sandbox.open(Path("[REDACTED:path]"))` sets `self.repo=/srv/sbx/repo` but `self.home=[REDACTED:path]`.

chunk_findings.detail: `agent_s = _held_s(ctx.facts, items, ctx.now) + _review_s(ctx.facts, items)` returns `0.0` when a repository has no `held` or `review` facts but has merged items (e.g., a sandbox/toy runner that records only completed states and no agent-hold records). The new metric `swarm.agent_hours_per_item` then emits `0.0` instead of `None`, and the new `text()` output prints `0.0000` under "agent-hours per item". That misrepresents absent measurement as a real zero agent-time figure; only `None` is rendered as `UNAVAILABLE`, so the view claims zero work was done rather than "unavailable", skewing the cost figure the change is supposed to model.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm_metrics.py provider

chunk_findings.detail: `judge` always returns `"compare": S.compare(before, after)` even when `comparable` is false. Concrete input: two sandboxes run with `--work-s 2` and `--work-s 4` produce a `why_not` entry for `work_s differs`, so the report says `"comparable": false`, but `report --json` still contains `compare.targets.throughput`, `compare.targets.rework`, and `compare.targets.cost` verdicts. A JSON consumer can read a target verdict for a pair the function says is not judged, contradicting the function's own contract and `render`'s human view.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:judge

chunk_findings.detail: There is no `lanes >= 1` validation. `python demos/swarm_pilot_run.py run DIR --lanes 0` (or a negative count) writes `lanes: 0` into the manifest, creates zero threads, sees no board failure, prints `ran 0 lane(s)`, and exits 0. This falsely records a sandbox as successfully run with no work done; the CLI should refuse non-positive lane counts.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: Unlike `guard_new`, `Sandbox.open` never rejects a path that is an ancestor of `ROOT`. Input: host repository is `[REDACTED:path]`; create `[REDACTED:path]` as its own git work tree with no remote and place `[REDACTED:path]` there. `Sandbox.open(Path("[REDACTED:path]"))` resolves the path, sees it is not inside the host, sees the manifest exists, passes `check()`, and returns a `Sandbox`. A subsequent `sb.ddflow("task", "add", ...)` runs `ddflow --repo [REDACTED:path]`, whose work tree contains the host repository, so the sandbox is not isolated from the host.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.open

chunk_findings.detail: The task-add loop adds every item with `--phase` and either `--needs <deps>` or `--tags no-deps`, but it never supplies a `wave:N` tag and never runs `ddflow waves --stamp`. This violates [r-task-phase-needs-wave], which requires every task to carry a `wave:N` tag; `no-deps` is not that wave tag. Running `setup()` on a fresh path creates 12 tasks without the required wave tag.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:setup

chunk_findings.detail: The documented agent-hours formula is “lease-held time plus recorded review time.” But the same document’s lane sequence is `claim`, `gate record` and `gate run`, `merge`, `complete`: a review recorded by `gate run` happens before `merge`, while the item is still lease-held. That review time is therefore already inside lease-held time, so adding it again double-counts it. Any real-lane run with a review gate (the setup this document explicitly tells SW-pilot-local to enable) inflates `swarm.agent_hours_per_item` and the `swarm_metrics.compare` `cost_x` ratio. The figure should not sum the two intervals; it should use a non-overlapping calculation such as lease-held time only, or subtract review time from lease-held time before adding it.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/swarm-pilot-toy.md:50

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `"cost_usd" in ans.text` only proves the label appears. A regressed view that still prints a skewed dollar figure (for example `cost_usd: 1.3`) when the log records no dollars would satisfy this test even though the comment claims it verifies “no dollars are recorded, and the view says so.” The test never asserts the value is `n/a` or absent, so the exact skewed-figure regression this change is meant to prevent is not caught.

chunk_findings.detail: `_git` runs `git -C <repo> ...` with whatever environment the pytest process inherited, without removing `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`. In an environment where these variables point at the host repository (the exact `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` attack the sandbox guard is supposed to neutralize), `git -C` does not override them. Concretely, in `test_a_linked_worktree_with_a_manifest_is_refused`, `_git(main, "worktree", "add", "-q", str(linked))` would add `<tmp>/linked` as a worktree of the **host** repository, mutating the host `.git/worktrees` metadata. This makes the new test suite itself touch the host under that environment, directly refuting the “sandbox never touches the host” guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py:_git

chunk_findings.detail: `_isolated` treats every non-zero `git cat-file -e` as "HEAD is unknown to the host". It also runs that probe with `env=sb.env`, so a sandbox env that makes host git fail (empty `PATH`, bad `GIT_EXEC_PATH`, `safe.directory` rejection, `GIT_DIR` pointing at a missing path) yields returncode 128/127, not 1. Given a sandbox whose `main` is a host commit and `git remote` is empty, `_isolated` returns True, `judge` sets `comparable`, and `render` can print throughput/rework `met` for a tree that is not isolated from the host.

chunk_findings.detail: `run` builds lanes with `range(1, lanes + 1)` and treats an empty thread list as success. `python3 demos/swarm_pilot_run.py run DIR --lanes 0` (or `--lanes -1`) writes the manifest, starts no workers, never calls `Board.over`, leaves every item undone, and exits 0 with `ran 0 lane(s)`.

chunk_findings.detail: `Board.over` reads and sorts `self.left` outside `self.lock`, then calls `fail` before re-checking under the lock. If the deadline fires as the last lane `finish`es the last item, `over` still records `deadline: N item(s) left` and `run` raises `RunFailed` after a complete phase. Concurrent `discard` during `sorted(self.left)` can also raise `RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration` and fail the run the same way.

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.__init__` stores any path and `git`/`ddflow` never call `check` or `guard_new`. `Sandbox(ROOT).must("merge", "toy-01")` runs `python -m ddflow --repo <host>` with the host checkout as `--repo`, so the sandbox harness mutates the host repository. The comments claim construction only through `setup`/`open`; that is not enforced on the methods that actually spawn processes.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:156

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.open` refuses a path inside the host but not a path that contains the host (`host.is_relative_to(real)` is only in `guard_new`). Given host `/work/proj` and an outer git repo `/work` with no remotes and `.ddflow/local/swarm-pilot.json` present, `Sandbox.open(Path("/work"))` succeeds, then `git`/`ddflow --repo /work` operate on a work tree that holds the host checkout.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:162

chunk_findings.detail: `clean_env` copies `TMPDIR` and `PATH` from the parent process. With `TMPDIR` set to a directory inside the host (for example `$HOST/tmp`) and `setup(Path("/tmp/pilot-sb"))` otherwise passing `guard_new`, `git` and the ddflow child still use that `TMPDIR` and can create files in the host. A `PATH` entry inside the host is also executed when resolving `git`/`python`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:82

chunk_findings.detail: The probe now passes the bare object name from `git rev-parse main` to `git -C ROOT cat-file -e`, dropping the previous `<sha>^{commit}` peel. If a sandbox has an annotated tag named `main` pointing to a commit the host already has, `git rev-parse main` resolves to the tag object, not the commit. The host lacks that local tag object, so `cat-file -e <tagSHA>` returns 1, `_isolated` returns True, and a pair is marked not comparable even though the host actually knows the commit. This false non-comparable verdict is exactly the kind the peel previously prevented.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:_isolated

chunk_findings.detail: The new allow-list checks only `argv[0]`, but not the `cwd` argument, so the constructor’s `apart_from_host` guard is bypassable on every git spawn. Concretely, after opening a valid sandbox `sb = Sandbox.open(Path("/tmp/pilot-sb"))`, calling `sb.git("add", "-A", cwd=ROOT)` runs `git -C <host> add -A` because `"add"` is in `GIT_VERBS` and `cwd or self.repo` resolves to the host repository. That mutates the host index despite the sandbox being valid and apart from the host.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: `self.repo` is passed through `apart_from_host`, but `self.home` is not resolved or checked before being installed as `TMPDIR` (and `HOME`) by the new `clean_env`. A sibling symlink `/tmp/evil.home -> <host>/tmp` next to a valid sandbox `/tmp/evil` is accepted by `Sandbox.open`; `sb.env["TMPDIR"]` is that symlink path, so any child that honors `TMPDIR` creates its temporary files inside the host repository, directly defeating the stated “TMPDIR … stay out of the host” isolation.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.__init__/clean_env

chunk_findings.detail: `sb.git("config")` raises an unhandled `IndexError` instead of `Refused`: since `argv[0] == "config"` is in `GIT_VERBS`, the condition evaluates `not argv[1].startswith("user.")`, and there is no `argv[1]`. The method’s own contract says an off-list call is `Refused`, but this banned one-argument `config` call crashes the harness.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: The test creates the link it exercises inside the real host checkout: `link = ROOT / ".ddflow" / f"pilot-link-{os.getpid()}"` mutates the host repository during the test. In an environment where pytest-xdist runs multiple workers against the same checkout, another worker's host `git status` can observe an untracked symlink under `.ddflow`; if the test process is killed before the `finally` cleanup, the symlink remains. This is the same host mutation the sandbox guard is supposed to prevent, and the test would avoid it by monkeypatching `T.ROOT` to a fresh temporary root instead of writing into the real `ROOT`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py:test_a_link_in_the_host_keeps_home_and_temp_files_out_of_it

chunk_findings.detail: This new test is meant to assert the `Board.over` lock fix, but it never creates the interleaving that made the old code fail. It calls `board.finish("toy-01")` before `board.over()`, so `self.left` is already empty when `over` runs, and no concurrent `discard` or deadline firing is exercised. The pre-fix implementation described in the earlier finding (`if not self.left: return True` before the deadline branch) also returns `True` with `failure == ""` for this exact sequential sequence, so the test passes on the buggy code and cannot catch a regression to reading `left` outside the lock or reporting a deadline when the last item completes concurrently.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py:test_a_finished_board_never_reports_a_deadline

chunk_findings.detail: `(before["lanes"] or 0) >= (after["lanes"] or 0)` turns a missing or non-positive baseline lane count into 0, so it passes the new “fewer before” rule whenever after has any positive count. chunk_findings.detail: The documented agent-hours formula is “lease-held time plus recorded review time.” But the same document’s lane sequence is `claim`, `gate record` and `gate run`, `merge`, `complete`: a review recorded by `gate run` happens before `merge`, while the item is still lease-held. That review time is therefore already inside lease-held time, so adding it again double-counts it. Any real-lane run with a review gate (the setup this document explicitly tells SW-pilot-local to enable) inflates `swarm.agent_hours_per_item` and the `swarm_metrics.compare` `cost_x` ratio. The figure should not sum the two intervals; it should use a non-overlapping calculation such as lease-held time only, or subtract review time from lease-held time before adding it.

chunk_findings.detail: The documented agent-hours formula is “lease-held time plus recorded review time.” But the same document’s lane sequence is `claim`, `gate record` and `gate run`, `merge`, `complete`: a review recorded by `gate run` happens before `merge`, while the item is still lease-held. That review time is therefore already inside lease-held time, so adding it again double-counts it. Any real-lane run with a review gate (the setup this document explicitly tells SW-pilot-local to enable) inflates `swarm.agent_hours_per_item` and the `swarm_metrics.compare` `cost_x` ratio. The figure should not sum the two intervals; it should use a non-overlapping calculation such as lease-held time only, or subtract review time from lease-held time before adding it.

chunk_findings.detail: `(before["lanes"] or 0) >= (after["lanes"] or 0)` turns a missing or non-positive baseline lane count into 0, so it passes the new “fewer before” rule whenever after has any positive count. A pair with `before["lanes"]` of `None`, `0`, or `-1` and `after["lanes"]` of `4` (same worker, work_s, and items, all merged) gets no lanes entry in `why`, so `judge` sets `comparable` true and keeps target verdicts. That scores an unmeasured or illegal baseline as the low-lane side; only a real positive count smaller than after should satisfy the check.

chunk_findings.detail: `git()` treats any argv whose second token starts with `user.` as a safe `config` verb, and then forwards the rest unchanged. `sb.git("config", "user.email", "[REDACTED:email]", "--file", str(ROOT / ".git" / "config"))` therefore passes the allow-list and runs `git -C <sandbox> config user.email [REDACTED:email] --file <host>/.git/config`, which writes the host git config. The comment that a listed verb cannot point git at another repository is false for `--file` (and the same pattern with `--file` before a later `user.*` key is the only reason the second-token check exists).
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:189

chunk_findings.detail: `apart_from_host` never checks `home`, but `clean_env` sets both `HOME` and `TMPDIR` to `repo.parent / f"{repo.name}.home"`. Host `/data/repos/pilot.home` and sandbox `/data/repos/pilot` fail neither `is_relative_to` test (`pilot.home` is not under `pilot`), yet `self.home` is exactly the host work tree. A later `git config` or temp file then lands in the host (`$HOME/.gitconfig`), which is the leak the TMPDIR/PATH change claims to close.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:169

chunk_findings.detail: The new lane-count validation `isinstance(n, int) and n >= 1` treats a JSON `true` as a valid lane count because `bool` is a subclass of `int` in Python. Given `before["lanes"] = True` and `after["lanes"] = 4` with equal `worker`, `work_s`, and `items`, and both sides fully merged, `_why_not` returns an empty list: `all(...)` is true for `True`, and `True >= 4` is false. `judge` then marks the pair comparable and scores a baseline whose lane count is not an integer of at least 1, exactly what the new rule says to reject.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:_why_not

chunk_findings.detail: This regression test does not exercise the prior `_isolated` non-peel bug it is claimed to guard. It creates an annotated tag `main` in `sb.repo`, then sets `T.ROOT` to that same `sb.repo`, so the “host” repository contains both the commit and the annotated tag object. The pre-fix implementation (`git -C ROOT cat-file -e <tagSHA>`) would also exit 0 here and pass `assert not R._isolated(sb)`, because the tag object exists locally in `ROOT`. The bug scenario requires a host that owns the commit but lacks the local tag; as written, the test would have passed on the unfixed code, so it cannot catch a regression of the original false non-comparable result.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py:test_a_tag_named_main_does_not_hide_a_known_commit

chunk_findings.detail: `--lanes` is an unconstrained int. `run(sb, 0, worker)` (CLI: `run DIR --lanes 0`, also any `lanes < 1`) builds an empty thread list, never calls `Board.over`, leaves `board.failure` empty, and returns success after writing `lanes` into the manifest. The sandbox is then marked already-run, so a later real run is refused, while no item was claimed or merged.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:run

chunk_findings.detail: `over` reads and `sorted(self.left)` outside `self.lock` while `finish` discards from that set. With the deadline already passed and at least one item still in `left`, one lane in `over` and another in `finish` makes `sorted` raise `RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration`. That exception is caught in `_lane` and stored as the run failure, so a run that actually finished every item is reported as `RunFailed`. The same unlocked check can call `fail` after the last `finish`, which also sets `failure` on a completed board.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:Board.over

chunk_findings.detail: `_why_not` never requires the two sides to differ in `lanes`, and `judge` always attaches `S.compare` (including target booleans) even when `why_not` is non-empty. `report A B --json` therefore emits `compare.targets` as met/NOT MET for two equal-lane sandboxes, or for a pair with overrides / a non-isolated sandbox, while the text path prints `NOT COMPARABLE`. Swapping a 1-lane and a 3-lane directory judges the throughput target in the wrong direction with no refusal.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:judge

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.git` forwards every argument after `git -C <sandbox>`, and `check` only runs at open/setup, not on each call. `sb.git("--git-dir", "<host>/.git", "commit", ...)` (or `sb.git("config", "core.worktree", "<host>")` followed by a write) operates on the host repository even though path guards passed and the sandbox has no remote.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: `guard_new` refuses a directory that contains the host (`host.is_relative_to(real)`), but `open` does not. Given a parent of the host that is its own work tree, has `.ddflow/local/swarm-pilot.json`, and has no remotes, `open` succeeds; a later `git add` or task whose glob reaches the nested host tree writes the host checkout.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.open

chunk_findings.detail: The allow-list copies `TMPDIR` unchanged. With `TMPDIR` set to a directory inside the host repository, every sandbox `git`/`ddflow` process inherits that path and can create temp files in the host tree, which the “never touches the host” guard never checks.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:clean_env

chunk_findings.detail: `open` passes the raw `path` to `cls`, and `__init__` resolves it only for `self.repo` (`self.repo = apart_from_host(repo)`), while `self.home` is still computed from the unresolved parameter `repo`. If `path` is a symlink inside the host repository that points to an external sandbox, `apart_from_host` accepts the resolved target, but `self.home` becomes `<host-dir>/<symlink-name>.home` inside the host. `clean_env` then sets both `HOME` and `TMPDIR` to that host path, so sandbox temp files can be written into the host tree despite the guard. Example: host `[REDACTED:path]`, symlink `[REDACTED:path] -> /srv/sbx/repo`, valid manifest at the target; `Sandbox.open(Path("[REDACTED:path]"))` sets `self.repo=/srv/sbx/repo` but `self.home=[REDACTED:path]`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.__init__ (with Sandbox.open)

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added `apart_from_host` guard applies only to `self.repo`; this diff leaves `Sandbox.git` unchanged, so it still forwards every caller argument after `git -C <self.repo>`. The constructor guard does not prevent argument-level redirection to the host repository: `sb.git("--git-dir", f"{ROOT}/.git", "commit", ...)` still operates on the host repository even though path guards passed, so the previously reported host-reachable `git` route remains.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier equal-lane / swapped-lane defect is still there. This delta only blanks `compare["targets"]` when `_why_not` is already non-empty; it never requires the two sides to differ in `lanes`, and it never checks which side is the multi-lane run. `judge` of two sandboxes that both have `lanes=3` (or a 1-lane directory passed as `after` and a 3-lane directory as `before`) still returns `comparable` true and real target booleans, so throughput is scored in the wrong direction with no refusal.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:judge

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier host-repo escape is not touched in this delta. `Sandbox.git` still appends every caller argument after `git -C <sandbox>`, and `check` still runs only at open/setup. `sb.git("--git-dir", "<host>/.git", "commit", ...)` or `sb.git("config", "core.worktree", "<host>")` followed by a write still operates on the host checkout after the path guards have passed.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: `__init__` stores the resolved repo but builds `home` from the unresolved argument, and `clean_env` now pins `TMPDIR` and `HOME` to that string. Given host `/work/repo` and symlink `/work/repo/out` → `/tmp/sb`, `Sandbox(Path("/work/repo/out"))` sets `self.repo` to `/tmp/sb` (apart_from_host allows it) and `self.home` to `/work/repo/out.home`. The next sandbox `git`/`ddflow` creates temp files and config under the host tree, which neither `apart_from_host` nor the TMPDIR allow-list checks.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:164

chunk_findings.detail: The new allow-list checks only `argv[0]` (and for `config`, `argv[1]`) but leaves the `cwd` parameter unvalidated and passes it directly to `git -C <cwd>`. Given an external sandbox `sb`, `sb.git("add", ".", cwd=ROOT)` passes the guard (`"add"` is in `GIT_VERBS`) and runs `git -C <host-repo> add .`, modifying the host repository index even though the sandbox itself is outside the host. This is the same host-reachable git route the change is meant to close, but it remains reachable through `cwd`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: The new check `(before["lanes"] or 0) >= (after["lanes"] or 0)` turns both `None` and `0` into `0`. For a baseline manifest missing `lanes` (or an old already-run sandbox created before `lanes < 1` was refused) against a valid after side such as `_side(lanes=3, per_hour=9.0)`, the condition is false and no lane reason is appended. If the default `worker`/`work_s`/`items`/`merged` fields align, `_why_not` is empty and `judge` reports the pair comparable and emits target verdicts, contrary to the intent that a non-comparable pair has `None` verdicts and that lanes under 1 are refused.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:_why_not

chunk_findings.detail: `Sandbox.git` only allow-lists `argv[0]` (and a `user.*` key). It still runs `git -C` on `cwd or self.repo`, and `cwd` is an unchecked caller argument. `sb.git("add", ".", cwd=ROOT)` (or `commit`) therefore writes the host checkout after the verb guard has passed. The new tests only pass `--git-dir` / `core.worktree` / `push` as leading arguments, so they do not catch this.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:193

chunk_findings.detail: `(before["lanes"] or 0) >= (after["lanes"] or 0)` treats a missing count as 0. Given `before["lanes"] is None` and `after["lanes"] == 3` (the same side shape as `_side(lanes=None)`), the comparison is `0 >= 3`, so this guard does not append a reason. A baseline with no lane count is then treated as having fewer lanes than a real multi-lane run, which is the wrong direction of the invariant the tests claim to lock (they only cover `(3,1)`, `(3,3)`, and `(None, None)`).
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:240

chunk_findings.detail: The guard indexes `argv[0]` and, for `config`, `argv[1]` with no length check. `sb.git()` raises `IndexError` before `Refused`; `sb.git("config")` does the same because `"config"` is an allowed verb and the `or` then evaluates `argv[1]`.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:190

chunk_findings.detail: `git` is launched with `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)` and no `env=self.env`. The new `clean_env` moves the committer identity into `self.env` (`GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`, `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`, `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`, `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`), but `sb.git("commit", "-m", ...)` does not inherit those variables. In an environment without a global git `user.name`/`user.email`, the harness's initial sandbox commit exits 128 and setup fails. The same missing `env` also inherits the caller's `GIT_*` variables; for example `GIT_DIR=<host>/.git GIT_WORK_TREE=<host>` with `sb.git("add", "/host/file")` passes the new `tree.is_relative_to(self.repo)` guard because `tree` is the sandbox, but the git process stages a host file.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_toy.py:Sandbox.git

chunk_findings.detail: `isinstance(n, int)` returns True for Python booleans, and JSON manifests can contain `true`. With `before["lanes"] == True` and `after["lanes"] == 3`, the new check treats `True` as the integer `1`, sees `1 < 3`, and appends no lane reason, so `judge` reports the pair comparable and emits target verdicts instead of NOT COMPARABLE. The requirement is that both lane counts be integers of at least 1, which a JSON boolean is not; the check should reject `bool` explicitly.
chunk_findings.title: demos/swarm_pilot_run.py:240

chunk_findings.detail: The test cannot catch the regression it was added for. It creates the annotated tag `main` inside `sb.repo`, then sets `T.ROOT = sb.repo`. If `_isolated` regresses to resolving `main` without peeling it to a commit, that returns the tag object; because `T.ROOT` is the same repository, the tag object is present there too, so the “host knows this object” check succeeds and `_isolated` returns False. The assertion `assert not R._isolated(sb)` then passes, even though the code still does not peel `main` to a commit. The host would need to contain the underlying commit but not the annotated tag for this test to detect the bug.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_pilot_toy.py:test_a_tag_named_main_does_not_hide_a_known_commit
